Private deferred exit reason prerequisite, not a wire implementation.

The raw reason bytes are owned without parsing. The preparation winner first executes a caller-supplied target/link decision. A dropped decision never invokes the decoder or malformed-reason callback. A selected reason uses the actual runtime ImportExternalTerm admission at decode time; its temporary epochs, captured identifier factories and final foreign-domain validation remain the existing production implementation. Cached completion prevents a second decoder or close callback. Runtime and caller-declared mailbox gate checks reject an unsafe first preparation before claiming the reason. No private lock is held during either callback or decode.

The malformed callback belongs to a future captured connection generation; this class does not close a connection or claim a queue statistic. A callback eligibility failure is a HOST failure and does not become a malformed external reason. A private unsupported decode also stays a private feature gap. Disposing an unclaimed reason drops it without decoding; disposing a running preparation does not cancel its callback. Ordered owner signal integration and cancellation/lifecycle coupling remain unimplemented.

No raw packet opcode, public BIF, existing process signal hook, or registry is changed. An ordered owner stage is still needed: ProcessInfo currently reenters AdmitSignals while holding the global gate, and Mailbox pending callbacks execute under both gates. Calling this helper from that old path is deliberately rejected. Merely using a background Task to complete it would reorder signals and is not proposed as a solution.

The returned Used count is retained without guessing native trailing-byte policy. Original payload11 observations are independent source-only work. This source has not yet been built or executed.

Revision2 adds a real captured connected-generation failure callback and private HOST source controls for dropped/owned/replayed/malformed/gated reasons and actual stale/new connection state with controller kill. These controls are source-only, not yet built or executed. A cached pending preparation is also refused under forbidden gates to prevent a blocked caller from holding a lock needed by the decoder. Existing public process_info and signal admission are unchanged; their faithful integration must release locks and preserve order rather than propagate this private misuse rejection.

# Erlang.Net

An experimental C#/.NET implementation targeting Erlang/OTP **29.1.1**, pinned to `ad05823719d77c8faee87348ea39513d4e2f99c5`. The full assignment is not complete. See [progress](docs/PROGRESS.md), [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), [detailed changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [next steps](docs/NEXT_STEPS.md).

Development validation now compares **778 expressions**, **4027 comparable separately compiled fixture modules** and **132 compiler-diagnostic fixtures** against the pinned reference. The module track compiles generated C# Release assemblies and reference BEAM modules; selected outcomes match, full optimizer/debug/resource compatibility remains unfinished. [Verified evidence](docs/validation/part-214/strict-guard.json).

Two map iterator fixtures explicitly use `-compile(no_ssa_opt)` because the pinned OTP optimizer assumes a map-only argument for `maps:map/2`. The initial optimized differences and one corrected provisional record-guard expectation remain documented in [the original comparison](docs/validation/part-102/differential.json) and [the source audit](docs/validation/part-104/reference-audit.json).

The implemented subset runs on .NET 10 without BEAM. It includes immutable terms, selective receive, local processes/links/monitors, an Erlang parser and evaluator, generated C# modules, selected Erlang gen_server/supervisor callback adapters and a mixed C#/Erlang MSBuild preprocessor.

All 91 lists exports are registered and directly tested; [lists compatibility scope](docs/LISTS_COMPATIBILITY.md) records functional proof and runtime boundaries.

All 34 maps exports are registered and directly tested; [maps compatibility scope](docs/MAPS_COMPATIBILITY.md) describes functional proof and remaining runtime boundaries.

Selected Erlang behaviour adapters expose ten gen_server and fourteen supervisor entry points. See [adapter usage and limitations](docs/OTP_ADAPTERS.md).

[Module readiness](docs/MODULE_READINESS.md) reports delivered/remaining component milestones, tested registered MFAs and changes from the previous checkpoint. Its API-presence percentages measure declarations, not complete compatibility. The full inventory is in [module-readiness.json](docs/module-readiness.json).

Regenerate the report from the current successful test report and actual runtime registry:

```powershell
dotnet run --project tools/Erlang.Tool --no-build -- readiness docs artifacts/tests.json docs
```

Term.A("ok") represents the Erlang atom ok, a symbolic value often used as a success marker; Term.String("ok") creates a character list. The factory reuses ten fixed common immutable atom values and leaves arbitrary Atom objects uncached; their names are retained in the VM-wide name table for existing-atom conversion. Compare terms by value, not CLR object identity. Domain constants retain their separate protocol meanings.

The source subset includes map construction, associative/exact updates and map patterns with supported guard-expression keys, plus integer/binary bitstring construction and patterns with signed extraction, byte order and prior-segment size bindings. Overall project completion is estimated at roughly 10% after the verified early functional platform milestone; this is an engineering estimate, not verified compatibility coverage. See progress and the changelog for evidence and remaining scope.

```powershell
dotnet build
dotnet run --project tests/Erlang.Tests --no-build -- artifacts/tests.json
dotnet run --project examples/HelloHybrid --no-build
```

The example prints `Hello World`, receives a stop message, and checks a compiled `.erl` module returning 42. Native Erlang syntax appears in an ordinary `.cs` file:

```csharp
var result = receive
    {hello, Name} when is_list(Name) ->
        io:format("Hello ~s~n", [Name]), ok;
    {stop} -> stop
end.
```

The enclosing method/lambda must be async and supply `ProcessContext erlangProcess`. Erlang constructs currently begin at C# statement/assignment/return/lambda-body boundaries; `end.` terminates each block. Blocks are independent Erlang scopes. C# locals are not implicitly imported into them. Synchronous suspension, arbitrary nested hybrid expressions and IDE language services are pending.

SDK 10.0.400 is pinned in `global.json`. On restricted hosts that prevent MSBuild worker processes, use `dotnet build -m:1`.

Compile Erlang source to C#:

```powershell
dotnet tools/Erlang.Tool/bin/Debug/net10.0/Erlang.Tool.dll compile examples/HelloHybrid/arithmetic.erl artifacts/arithmetic.g.cs
```

Generate the pinned source inventory without changing the reference checkout:

```powershell
dotnet tools/Erlang.Tool/bin/Debug/net10.0/Erlang.Tool.dll inventory ../otp docs
```

Validate build integration and a local NuGet consumer:

```powershell
pwsh -File tools/validate.ps1
```

No packages are published. The prototype package targets net10.0. Install the local tool package to run `dotnet erlang compile INPUT OUTPUT`; without installation, use the DLL command above. Compilation currently emits AST construction code evaluated by the C# runtime, rather than direct native lowering of every operation.

Source formatting: `dotnet run --project tools/Erlang.Style -- --write .`. The full validation script checks layout with `--check`. This development tool uses the pinned SDK's Roslyn formatter and repository-specific spacing/argument rules; it does not process native-Erlang hybrid Program.cs. Detailed numbered work history is indexed in [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md); append only to its latest volume, rolling over at 32 KiB or 400 lines.

Tests are a dependency-free executable harness and return a failing exit code on any failed assertion. `dotnet test` is not the test entry point. A separate differential runner requires an exact OTP 29.1.1 development oracle; production execution and builds do not.

The erlang module currently registers **287/351** pinned exports; [scope ledger](docs/ERLANG_COMPATIBILITY.md) lists64 missing APIs. Real external-process ports include the13 port APIs, line/packet IO, owned monitors/aliases/priority/exit/link lifecycle, output and signal queue pressure, and actual in/out, shared stderr, argv0, auxiliary stdio and Windows overlapped options across170 source scenarios. [Part214](docs/validation/part-214/strict-guard.json) verifies4937/4937 original comparisons and5544/full same-head CI. The437 registered MFAs are directly tested;native drivers/fd, other executable formats/platforms, complete metadata/errno/GUI/resource/scheduling/distribution/upstream/performance contracts remain unfinished. API presence is not semantic completion.

Current fd increment: borrowed Linux descriptors/Windows handles have real pipe/file IO,packet/line/EOF and cancellation checks. Part215 original run completed4946/4951 with five new fd metadata/settings mismatches;the separate inherited fd track passed3/8. Part216 corrects os_pid to {os_pid,undefined} and rejects exit_status;5568/full Windows local checks pass,patched original proof is pending. See [repair and retained evidence](docs/changelog/0031.md). TTY/control/flag and broader resource/platform compatibility remain partial;API presence remains erlang287/351.

Corrected fd verification: [Part217](docs/validation/part-217/strict-guard.json) passes4951/4951 corpus plus8/8 inherited fd IO and5568/full exact-head Linux CI. Earlier initial failures are preserved in216;TTY/flags/ABI/resources/platform and whole erlang compatibility remain partial.

Selected spawn_opt verification: [Part219](docs/validation/part-219/strict-guard.json) passes4997/4997 corpus plus8/8 inherited fd IO and5618/full exact-head Linux CI. The additional fd IO remains passing;heap/GC/CPU priority/connected distribution and whole erlang compatibility remain partial.
